summary:
The video presents a Pinterest strategy that the creator, Megan (a recipe blogger), started implementing just after Christmas. She reports that her impressions and outbound clicks have been slowly increasing each week after declining throughout the previous quarter. She emphasizes the change was not about pinning more but about changing the approach to pinning.

The first step is keyword research using the free Pinterest Trends tool before designing any pins. The creator recommends using desktop rather than phone for this tool. After finishing a blog post, she searches the Pinterest Trends tool using the same keywords the post was structured around. She demonstrates with an example of a post called 'Small Entryway Organization Ideas for Busy Families.' Within the tool, clicking the magnifying glass labeled 'search trends' reveals a search bar where typing keywords shows prepopulated terms with search volume graphs. Setting the date range to one year shows seasonal patterns, and scrolling below the graph reveals Pinterest's related keyword recommendations.

The goal of the keyword research is to identify three sets of keywords total: the original blog post keywords plus two additional sets that will be used to create two new boards. In the example, she identifies 'small entryway ideas,' 'organization ideas for the home,' and 'small space organization' as her three keyword sets.

For pinning execution, the creator makes two pins for each of the three keyword sets, resulting in six total pins per blog post. All six pins link to the same URL but have different text overlays incorporating their respective target keywords. She pins to one existing established board and creates two new boards named exactly after the keyword sets. For board descriptions, she uses ChatGPT by telling it she's creating a new board, providing the target keywords, and asking for an SEO-optimized description to copy and paste.

The scheduling strategy involves not pinning all six pins at once. Instead, she uses Pinterest's free built-in scheduling tool to space pins one week apart, rotating through the three boards. For example: today to board A, one week later to board B, two weeks to board C, three weeks back to board A, and so on. This spacing gives Pinterest time to test each pin and prevents competing with yourself. The creator notes this is slow intentional growth rather than expecting viral results overnight. She works on this once weekly when finishing a post, and each post is then covered for 5-6 weeks without additional pinning. She attributes the success to consistency, noting this is the first time she has been really consistent with a Pinterest strategy.
